threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and initial backlog for the program.

messages.text:
Hi all, kicking off the Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing & Client Visit Program channel.
Goal: get a shared view on scope, what success looks like for the first three months, and who owns the first core tasks.
From the project_pack_ref Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing & Client Visit Program, the key early items are the wellbeing guidelines, the client visit playbook, the on-site checklist, and the central calendar (T1–T4). We also already have placeholder artifacts like the Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing Guidelines draft and Client Visit Playbook (A1, A2) that we will refine.
Can we use this thread to:
- confirm scope and success metrics for the first quarter
- agree owners and target dates for T1–T4
- surface any constraints or risks we should flag now

Tagging you here to get started.

Thanks for starting this.
From a client side, I suggest we keep scope for the first three months to:
- one pilot office
- a defined group of key accounts
- a limited set of wellbeing activities that we know we can deliver consistently.
For success metrics, I propose:
- client visit satisfaction average at or above 4.3 out of 5 (from the client survey that will sit in A1/A2 context)
- at least 80 percent of planned client visits in the calendar actually happening as scheduled (T4)
- at least one wellbeing touchpoint per client visit (e.g. short office tour aligned with the playbook in A2).
Curious what you think and how this fits with the wellbeing and operations angles.

From the wellbeing side, I would keep scope focused on simple, repeatable routines for hybrid work.
For the first three months, I suggest we limit A1 (Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing Guidelines) to:
- basic physical and ergonomic tips for on-site and remote days
- short mental health micro-break suggestions
- guidance on how client visits interact with quiet zones and focus time.
For success metrics, maybe we track:
- at least 70 percent of employees in the pilot office confirm they have seen the guidelines (via the survey later in A5)
- no reported incidents where a wellbeing activity or client visit clearly breached safety rules.
This should be realistic within the 21-day launch window.
Happy to own T1 and T5 content-wise, but I will need HR and operations to review for compliance as the backlog already states.

On logistics and coordination:
- For T3 (on-site client visit checklist) and T4 (centralised calendar), I can help structure the templates and align with our existing office systems.
- We should also keep an eye on the risk of overloading assistants. The project_pack_ref mentions this explicitly, so I would like to keep the checklist in A3 very concise and the calendar in A4 as automated as possible.
For success metrics, maybe we add:
- 100 percent of client visits in the pilot use the on-site checklist (A3)
- no more than two overlapping high-priority events per day in the shared calendar (A4).
If that sounds reasonable, I can draft a first version of T3 and T4 by early next week.

I can support on T3 and T4 as well, especially making sure the templates and calendar naming follow our internal communication style.
One question on scope: do we include remote-only client meetings in this first phase, or only physical visits to the office? It affects how we design the checklist in A3 and the playbook in A2.
My suggestion would be to keep the first three months focused on on-site visits only, and we can add a remote visit section later once the basics are running smoothly.

Good point on remote meetings.
I agree that for the first three months we should limit scope to on-site visits. Otherwise T2 and T7 will become too broad and we risk missing the 21-day launch target.
We can still add a short note in A2 that remote visits will be covered in a later update.
If no one objects, I will assume on-site only for this first phase.

On ownership and timing for T1–T4, here is a proposal based on the backlog:
- T1 wellbeing guidelines: owner 99128, with HR and operations review routed via assistants. Target: draft by day 7, final by day 14.
- T2 client visit playbook: owner 382239, with validation from 99128 and operations. Target: draft by day 9, final by day 16.
- T3 on-site client visit checklist: owner 507162, with review from 382239 and 99128. Target: draft by day 8, final by day 15.
- T4 centralised calendar: owner 425046, with access rules agreed with HR and sales. Target: structure by day 5, test event by day 10.
Does this work for everyone? If yes, we can lock this as our initial plan.

The proposal works for me.
For T3, I will start from the existing reception checklist and add the wellbeing and client experience elements we need, then share a short draft here for comments.
Timeline day 8 for draft and day 15 for final is fine.

I am ok to own T1 with the suggested dates.
To keep it realistic, I will:
- reuse some of our existing ergonomic and mental health material
- keep the first version of A1 short and practical
- flag any legal or HR questions so they can be picked up in T11 later.
I will also block time with HR to make sure we do not miss any safety or privacy requirements.

I am aligned with the ownership and dates for T2.
I will structure A2 around three phases: pre-visit, on-site, and follow-up, and I will plug in the wellbeing touchpoints you mentioned earlier.
I will also make sure T7 (client segmentation and visit priorities) is consistent with the calendar rules in T4 so we do not create conflicts.

I am happy with the plan as well.
I can support 425046 on T4 by checking that the calendar naming and color-coding are easy to understand for reception and managers.
On success metrics, can we summarise them in one place so we can reuse them later in the reporting template (A8)? I can help draft that summary if needed.

Good idea on summarising the metrics.
Let me recap what we have so far for the first three months:
- On-site visits only, one pilot office.
- Client satisfaction average at or above 4.3 out of 5.
- At least 80 percent of planned client visits executed as scheduled.
- At least one wellbeing touchpoint per client visit.
- At least 70 percent of employees confirm they have seen the guidelines.
- 100 percent of pilot client visits use the on-site checklist.
- No more than two overlapping high-priority events per day in the shared calendar.
If everyone is ok with this, we can treat this as our working definition of success and move on to detailed design in the other threads.

The summary looks good to me.
One small addition: for the 80 percent execution rate, I suggest we count rescheduled visits within the same month as ok, as long as they are still in the calendar (A4). Otherwise we might punish ourselves for reasonable client changes.
With that nuance, I am comfortable treating this as our success definition for the first three months.

I am aligned with the metrics and the on-site only scope.
From my side, I will make sure the surveys in A5 can capture the key data points we need for these metrics, especially awareness of A1 and perceived impact of the wellbeing touchpoints during visits.
No further changes from me.

Thanks all. Given the feedback, I suggest we formally lock:
- Scope: on-site client visits only, one pilot office, limited set of wellbeing activities.
- Success metrics: as summarised above, with the nuance on rescheduled visits within the same month.
- Ownership and target dates for T1–T4 as proposed.
Unless there are objections today, we will treat this as confirmed and use it as the baseline for the other threads.

No objections from me. I will proceed with T3 based on this scope and timing.
I will post the first draft checklist in the dedicated thread once ready.

All good from my side as well.
I will start drafting A2 and T2 with the agreed metrics and scope in mind so we can later connect them to the pilot in T10.

Aligned here too.
I will support on T4 and help document the metrics in a simple overview so we can plug them into A8 later.
Looking forward to seeing the drafts in the other threads.

threads.thread_goal: Define the client visit playbook and on-site checklist details.

messages.text:
As discussed, here is the first structure proposal for the Client Visit Playbook (A2) for the pilot.
Scope: on-site visits only, one pilot office, aligned with the wellbeing guidelines in A1.
Draft structure for T2:
1. Pre-visit
   - client selection and segmentation reference (T7)
   - visit objective and agenda template
   - pre-visit email to client, including short note on our wellbeing-friendly office
   - internal coordination with assistants and calendar (T4).
2. On-site
   - arrival and reception flow, linked to the on-site checklist (A3, T3)
   - office tour script with wellbeing touchpoints (quiet zones, ergonomic setups, break areas)
   - meeting room etiquette and safety basics.
3. Follow-up
   - thank-you email template with survey link (A5 later)
   - internal notes and next steps.
I would like feedback on whether this covers what you need and if anything is missing before we go into detailed wording.

Thanks for sharing the structure.
From an assistant and reception perspective, I like that the on-site part clearly links to A3.
For T3, I suggest we mirror your on-site section with a simple checklist structure:
- before client arrival (room setup, safety, refreshments, materials)
- at arrival (reception greeting, visitor badges, quick wellbeing note)
- during visit (support for room changes, technical issues)
- after visit (reset room, store checklist copy).
This way A2 and A3 stay in sync and easy to follow.

From the wellbeing angle, the structure looks good.
A few suggestions:
- In the pre-visit phase, add a short internal check to confirm that the planned visit does not clash with any high-intensity wellbeing activity (e.g. sessions that require quiet space). This can be a quick check in the calendar (A4).
- In the on-site phase, the office tour script should include a short explanation of how we support hybrid work routines, not only physical spaces.
- In the follow-up, we might want to include one or two wellbeing-related questions in the client survey (A5) so we can see how the visit experience lands.
I can help draft the wellbeing parts of the script once the structure is agreed.

I like the three-phase structure.
From a coordination and communication point of view, I would add:
- a short internal briefing template before the visit so everyone knows the client name, objectives, and any sensitivities
- a note on who is responsible for updating the central calendar (A4) and by when.
This will help assistants avoid last-minute surprises.

Agree with the comments so far.
To keep things manageable for reception and assistants, I would suggest:
- keep the on-site section in A2 high-level and let A3 carry the detailed steps
- clearly mark which steps are mandatory vs. nice-to-have, so we do not overload the team during busy days.
If we align on this, I think the structure is solid and we can move to wording.

Thanks for all the input.
Let me summarise the updated structure for A2 based on your feedback:
1. Pre-visit
   - client selection and segmentation reference (T7)
   - visit objective and agenda template
   - internal briefing template (client, objectives, sensitivities)
   - pre-visit email to client with wellbeing note
   - calendar and wellbeing conflict check (A4, A1).
2. On-site
   - arrival and reception flow, with link to A3
   - office tour script including hybrid work routines and wellbeing touchpoints
   - meeting room etiquette and safety basics
   - clear indication of mandatory vs. optional steps.
3. Follow-up
   - thank-you email with survey link (A5)
   - internal notes and next steps.
If everyone is comfortable with this, I would like to treat the structure as final and then fill in the content.

The updated structure works for me.
It gives us a clear anchor for T3, and we can keep the checklist very practical while still pointing back to A2 for context.
No further changes from my side.

Aligned here as well.
Once you lock the structure, I will draft the wellbeing parts of the office tour script and the wellbeing-related survey questions for A5 so they match the visit experience described in A2.

Looks good to me.
For the internal briefing template, I can help format it so assistants can quickly reuse it in emails or calendar invites.
No blockers from my side to move ahead.

Great, thanks all.
Given the feedback and no objections, I propose we formally approve this structure and key steps for the Client Visit Playbook (A2) and move into detailed drafting.
I will then share a near-final version for a quick check before we start the pilot.

Switching to the on-site checklist (A3) for T3, here is a simple structure proposal aligned with A2:
1. Before client arrival
   - room booked and visible in calendar (A4)
   - room clean and tidy
   - safety checks (exits visible, no cables on the floor)
   - refreshments prepared
   - materials ready (presentations, handouts, visitor badges).
2. At arrival
   - greet client and confirm agenda
   - provide visitor badge and basic safety note
   - mention wellbeing-friendly aspects briefly (e.g. break areas, quiet zones).
3. During visit
   - support room changes or technical issues
   - keep refreshments topped up if needed.
4. After visit
   - reset room
   - store completed checklist (digital or paper) for T10 reporting.
Please let me know if anything critical is missing before we freeze this for the pilot.

This covers the essentials from a client perspective.
Two small additions:
- In the pre-arrival section, add a check that the client name and company are correctly displayed at reception if we use screens or signs.
- In the after-visit section, add a reminder to trigger the follow-up email with the survey link (A5) and to log any key client comments.
With those, I think A3 will support the playbook well.

From the wellbeing side, I would only add:
- a quick ergonomic check in the room (chair height adjustable, screen at a comfortable distance)
- a note to offer water and, where appropriate, a short break during longer visits.
These are small touches but they support the wellbeing positioning of the program.

I agree with the additions.
To keep the checklist manageable for reception, maybe we can mark a few items as optional for very short visits (for example, the full office tour).
Otherwise, I think this version is ready to use in the pilot.

Thanks for the suggestions.
I will integrate:
- signage check at reception
- ergonomic and water check
- follow-up email reminder with survey link
- optional markers for very short visits.
Unless there are strong objections, I suggest we treat this as the final version of A3 for the pilot so we can start testing it with the first visits.

Works for me.
Having a stable version of A3 will also help us when we prepare the training session agenda (A7) and the reporting template (A8), since we can refer to concrete steps.
I support locking this version for the pilot.

Agreed.
Given the alignment, I suggest we formally lock both:
- the structure and key steps of the Client Visit Playbook (A2)
- the on-site client visit checklist (A3) for pilot use.
We can still refine wording later, but the flow and content are now stable enough for T10.

threads.thread_goal: Set up calendar, communication plan, and training session logistics.

messages.text:
Here is a proposal for the centralised calendar setup (A4, T4) and launch communications (A6, T6), plus a first idea for the training session logistics (A7, T8).
1) Calendar structure (A4, T4)
- Tool: use our existing shared calendar system, create one shared calendar named Hybrid Wellbeing & Client Visits.
- Color-coding:
  - dark blue: client visits
  - green: wellbeing activities
  - grey: internal training related to the program.
- Naming convention: [Client/Activity] - [Type] - [Owner initials].
- Access:
  - read access for all staff in the pilot office
  - edit access for assistants and account managers.
2) Launch communication plan (A6, T6)
- Day 14: launch email to pilot office employees in two languages, explaining the program and linking to A1 and A2.
- Day 15: short FAQ for employees and client-facing staff.
- Day 16–21: reminders in the weekly office newsletter.
3) Training session (A7, T8)
- 60-minute session for assistants and account managers.
- Agenda: overview of A1 and A2, walk-through of A3 and A4, quick look at surveys (A5) and reporting (A8), Q&A.
- Proposed date: day 17 at 10:00 in the pilot office meeting room.
Please review especially the calendar access rules and the training date before we confirm.

Thanks for laying this out.
On the calendar (A4, T4):
- I like the color-coding and naming convention, it should be easy to scan.
- For access, I would suggest we also give edit rights to reception, since they often handle last-minute changes.
On the training (A7, T8):
- Day 17 at 10:00 works for me, but we should check with sales to avoid clashes with key client calls.
I can help schedule the session once we confirm the date.

From the sales side, the calendar proposal looks workable.
Two small points:
- For client visits, could we add a short code for the client segment (from T7) in the title, for example [A] or [B]? That will help us later when we review the pilot.
- For access, I agree reception should have edit rights.
On the training date: day 17 at 10:00 is fine as long as we avoid overlapping with our weekly sales call. If we keep it to 60 minutes sharp, it should be ok.

On the launch communication (A6, T6):
- I like the idea of a day 14 email and a day 15 FAQ.
- Could we also include a short note about how employees can raise concerns or suggestions about wellbeing activities? That will connect nicely with the continuous improvement process in T12.
For the training (A7, T8), I am available on day 17 at 10:00 and can cover the wellbeing guidelines (A1) and survey basics (A5).

On the communication plan (A6, T6), I would suggest we:
- keep the launch email short and link to a one-page overview in A6 for those who want more detail
- add a short section in the FAQ about how client visits will be scheduled and how employees can see them in the calendar (A4).
For the calendar, I support giving reception edit rights and adding the client segment code in the title as 382239 suggested.

Thanks for the feedback.
Updated calendar proposal (A4, T4):
- Name: Hybrid Wellbeing & Client Visits.
- Color-coding: unchanged.
- Naming convention: [Client/Activity] - [Type] - [Segment code] - [Owner initials].
- Access: read for all staff in pilot office; edit for assistants, account managers, and reception.
On the communication plan (A6, T6):
- I will keep the launch email concise and link to a one-page overview.
- FAQ will include how to see visits in the calendar and how to raise wellbeing suggestions.
On the training (A7, T8):
- Day 17 at 10:00 still seems fine; I will double-check against the sales call and then book the slot.
If there are no strong objections, I suggest we adopt this calendar structure and access model.

The updated calendar setup works for me.
The segment code in the title will be very helpful later when we look at T7 and T10.
No further changes from my side.

Aligned as well.
Reception edit rights and the naming convention will make it easier for us to keep the calendar clean.
I am ok to proceed with this structure.

No objections from me.
The calendar structure is clear, and it will help avoid clashes between wellbeing activities and client visits.
I am ready to reference A4 in the wellbeing planning once it is live.

Given the alignment, I suggest we formally choose this calendar structure and access model as our standard for the pilot.
I will go ahead and create the calendar and share the link in A4 once done.

On the training session details (A7, T8), could we clarify the exact agenda and timeboxes? That will help us keep it within 60 minutes.
Proposal:
- 10 min: program overview and objectives (425046)
- 15 min: wellbeing guidelines and hybrid routines (99128, A1)
- 15 min: client visit playbook and checklist (382239 and 507162, A2 and A3)
- 10 min: calendar, surveys, and reporting (A4, A5, A8)
- 10 min: Q&A.
If this works, we can confirm the date and send the invite.

The agenda and timeboxes look good to me.
I can take the 15 minutes on the client visit playbook (A2) and coordinate with 507162 on how we present the checklist (A3) so it feels like one flow.

Works for me as well.
I will focus on the practical side of A3 and show how assistants and reception can use it together with the calendar (A4).

I am comfortable with 15 minutes for the wellbeing guidelines and hybrid routines.
I will prepare a short slide deck for A1 and a couple of examples of how wellbeing activities will show up in the calendar (A4) and surveys (A5).

Great, thanks for the quick alignment.
I have checked the sales calendar and day 17 at 10:00 does not clash with the weekly sales call.
I propose we confirm:
- training date: day 17
- duration: 60 minutes
- agenda as outlined by 548231.
I will book the session in the shared calendar (A4) and prepare the invite using A7 as the base.

Perfect.
Once the invite is out, I can help refine the A6 communication so it points people to the training session and clarifies who should attend.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on survey templates, compliance checks, and reporting format.

messages.text:
As promised, here is the first draft outline for the survey templates (A5, T5) and the continuous improvement process (T12), plus a proposal for the monthly reporting template (A8, T9).
1) Survey templates (A5, T5)
- Employee survey (quarterly):
  - awareness of wellbeing guidelines (A1)
  - perceived usefulness of wellbeing activities
  - experience with hybrid routines (on-site and remote)
  - open question for suggestions.
- Client survey (per visit, then summarised quarterly):
  - overall satisfaction with the visit
  - perception of the office environment and wellbeing aspects
  - clarity of agenda and logistics (A2, A3)
  - likelihood to recommend visiting again.
2) Continuous improvement process (T12)
- Data sources: surveys (A5), monthly status reports (A8), ad-hoc feedback.
- Roles:
  - I consolidate wellbeing-related feedback
  - sales consolidates client-related feedback
  - assistants flag operational issues.
- Cadence: monthly quick review, quarterly deeper review.
3) Monthly reporting template (A8, T9)
- Sections:
  - key activities (visits and wellbeing sessions)
  - attendance and basic metrics
  - issues and risks
  - improvement actions decided.
Please review the structure and suggest changes before we finalise the questions and format.

Thanks for kicking this off.
On the client survey in A5:
- I would add one question about whether the visit helped them understand how we support hybrid work and wellbeing, since that is a key message of A2.
- For the likelihood to recommend, we can use a 0–10 scale so we can later calculate a simple promoter score if needed.
On the monthly report (A8, T9), I suggest we include a small section for key client quotes, as those are often useful in sales conversations.

On the reporting template (A8, T9), from an operations and coordination view, I would add:
- a simple traffic-light status for the program (green/amber/red)
- a short note on calendar usage (A4): for example, percentage of visits and activities correctly logged.
This will help us quickly see if the basics are working without reading all the details.

From the assistants side, I like the idea of a monthly report but we should keep it light.
Maybe we can:
- limit the number of free-text fields in A8
- use checkboxes or short dropdowns where possible (for example, type of issue: scheduling, room setup, communication).
That will make it easier for us to fill in T9 regularly.

On the continuous improvement process (T12), I would suggest we:
- clearly state who leads the monthly quick review and who documents the decisions
- define where we store the summary (for example, in the same folder as A8) so we can track changes over time.
I can help set up a simple naming convention for those summaries.

Thanks for the input.
Updated proposal:
- I will lead the monthly quick review, with sales and assistants joining when needed.
- We will store the monthly summary in the same folder as A8, with a simple naming convention like Program Status - YYYY-MM.
- I will document the decisions and improvement actions in that summary.
On the surveys, I will integrate the extra client question about understanding our hybrid and wellbeing approach, and use a 0–10 scale for the recommendation question.

Sounds good to me.
One more point: for T11 (legal and compliance review), we should make sure both A1 and A5 go through HR/legal before we launch.
I can take care of sending the documents and tracking feedback, but I will need your final drafts first.

Agreed.
I will aim to have near-final drafts of A1 and A5 ready by day 12 so you can send them for HR/legal review under T11.
We should not publish any survey or guideline before we have that feedback, to avoid compliance issues.

On the client survey, one practical question: will the survey link be included in the follow-up email template in A2, or do we send it separately?
My preference is to include it in the standard follow-up email so we do not forget it after visits.

Including the survey link in the standard follow-up email makes sense.
We can also add a small reminder in the on-site checklist (A3) under the after-visit section to trigger that email, so it is not missed in busy days.

I will align with that.
The client survey link will be part of the standard follow-up email template in A2, and we will keep the reminder in A3 as you suggested.
This should help us reach the response rates we need for the pilot.

On the monthly reporting template (A8), do we want to fix a specific day each month for the review, for example the first Monday of the month? That might make it easier for everyone to plan.
If yes, we can note that in T12 so it is clear.

Good idea.
Let us set the monthly review on the first Monday of each month, using the latest A8 report as input.
I will add this to the T12 description so it is explicit.

From my side, the survey structures and the reporting template now cover what we need for the pilot and the first three months.
I am comfortable moving to final wording and then to HR/legal review for A1 and A5.

Same here.
The A8 template with the added traffic-light status and calendar usage note should give us a clear view each month without too much effort.
I suggest we treat the current survey structures and reporting template as final for the pilot, pending HR/legal review.

Given the alignment, I propose we formally approve the survey templates for employees and clients (A5) for the pilot, subject to HR/legal feedback, and adopt the monthly reporting template (A8) and review cadence as described.
I will finalise the wording and share the drafts with 425046 for T11.

threads.thread_goal: Run pilot debrief and decide adjustments before wider rollout.

messages.text:
Pilot debrief for the Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing & Client Visit Program.
Summary of T10 so far in the pilot office:
- Client visits: 3 completed (segments A, A, B) using the Client Visit Playbook (A2) and the on-site checklist (A3).
- Wellbeing activities: 2 sessions completed (one ergonomic micro-session, one short mindfulness break) aligned with A1.
- Surveys (A5):
  - Clients: 3 responses, average satisfaction 4.7 out of 5, average recommendation score 9 out of 10.
  - Employees: 12 responses so far; 75 percent say they have seen the wellbeing guidelines.
Operational notes:
- Calendar (A4) worked well, but we had one near-conflict between a wellbeing session and a last-minute client visit.
- Assistants reported that the checklist (A3) is helpful but a bit long for very short visits.
I would like us to use this thread to decide what we adjust before we roll out more widely, and to confirm that our initial scope and success metrics still make sense.

From the assistants side, a few observations:
- The on-site checklist (A3) works well for standard visits, but for 30-minute drop-ins it feels heavy.
- The reminder to send the follow-up email with the survey link is useful; we did not miss it.
- The calendar (A4) naming convention helped us quickly see which visits were part of the pilot.
Suggestion: we could create a short version of A3 for very short visits, or clearly mark which items are optional in those cases.

From the wellbeing perspective:
- The ergonomic micro-session was well received; employees mentioned they appreciated the practical tips.
- The mindfulness break had lower attendance, possibly due to timing close to a client visit.
- No safety incidents were reported.
On the surveys (A5), the employee responses show that some people still do not know where to find the guidelines (A1), so we may need a small reminder in the internal communication plan (A6) or in team meetings.

On coordination and communication:
- The shared calendar (A4) mostly worked, but the near-conflict you mentioned shows we should tighten the rule about booking wellbeing sessions during peak client times.
- Some employees asked whether they could see which visits are part of the wellbeing pilot vs. regular visits; maybe we can add a small tag in the event title.
I can help adjust the calendar guidelines and the FAQ in A6 accordingly.

Thanks for the summary.
Looking at our initial success metrics from TH1:
- client satisfaction above 4.3: we are at 4.7, so on track.
- at least 80 percent of planned visits executed: all 3 pilot visits happened as scheduled, so 100 percent.
- at least one wellbeing touchpoint per visit: confirmed for all 3.
- at least 70 percent of employees aware of the guidelines: we are at 75 percent in the early survey sample.
- 100 percent of pilot visits using the checklist: confirmed.
- no more than two overlapping high-priority events per day: we had a near-conflict but no actual overlap.
Based on this, I would say the initial scope and metrics still make sense, but we should fine-tune the checklist and calendar rules before scaling.

I agree with that assessment.
From client conversations, the wellbeing angle was noticed and appreciated, especially the ergonomic setup and the calm meeting environment.
I would keep the overall scope and metrics as they are for the first three months, and focus our adjustments on:
- simplifying A3 for short visits
- clarifying calendar rules in A4 to avoid conflicts
- reinforcing communication about where to find A1.
If we align on this, we can confirm the original scope and metrics and move to concrete tweaks.

On simplifying A3, I propose we:
- keep the current checklist as the standard version
- add a short section at the top: For visits under 45 minutes, focus on these core items only.
That way we do not need a separate document, but assistants know what to prioritise when time is tight.

For communication about A1, I can prepare a short reminder paragraph that we can include in the next internal newsletter and in team meeting notes.
We can also add a line in the training materials (A7) to remind assistants and account managers to point colleagues to the guidelines when questions come up.

On the calendar rules in A4, I suggest we:
- block a few core time slots per week where we avoid scheduling wellbeing sessions, to keep space for last-minute client visits
- add a simple rule in the FAQ: if in doubt, client visits take priority, and wellbeing sessions can be moved.
This should reduce the risk of conflicts without making planning too rigid.

I like these suggestions.
To move us forward, I propose we:
- keep the original scope and success metrics for the first three months as defined in TH1
- adjust A3 with a short-priority section for visits under 45 minutes
- update A4 guidelines to include protected slots and the rule that client visits take priority
- reinforce communication about A1 in A6 and A7.
If everyone agrees, we can treat this as our pilot adjustment package.

Aligned.
Given the pilot results and the discussion, I am comfortable confirming the original scope and success metrics for the first three months, with the small operational tweaks you listed.
This gives us a stable baseline to communicate to stakeholders.

I support the plan.
I will take care of updating A3 with the short-visit priority section and will start using it in the next visits.
